_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Based on the Mumble egg in https://github.com/pelican-eggs/voice (MIT).
name: Mumble
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Mumble is an open source, low-latency voice chat for gaming. Runs the official Mumble server, with the user limit, password and SuperUser password set from the server's settings.
startup: if [ -n "$SUPERUSER_PASSWORD" ]; then mumble-server -ini murmur.ini -supw "$SUPERUSER_PASSWORD" 2>&1 | grep -i superuser; fi; exec mumble-server -fg -ini murmur.ini

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Mumble: the server program comes with the runtime image, so this only
# writes a starting murmur.ini. An existing murmur.ini and the database
# (murmur.sqlite, with channels, users and certificates) are kept.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

if [ -f murmur.ini ]; then
    echo "murmur.ini is already here: keeping it."
else
    cat > murmur.ini <<'CONF'
; Mumble server settings: https://www.mumble.info/documentation/administration/config-file/
; The port, user limit, password and welcome message are set by the
; server's settings.
database=murmur.sqlite
logfile=
port=64738
host=
users=100
serverpassword=
welcometext="Welcome to this Mumble server."
bandwidth=558000
timeout=30
textmessagelength=5000
imagemessagelength=131072
allowhtml=true
opusthreshold=0
sendversion=true
CONF
    echo "Wrote murmur.ini."
fi
echo "Installed Mumble's settings. Start the server to create its database."

variables.name: Max users
variables.description: The most people who can be connected at once.

variables.name: Server password
variables.description: A password everyone needs to join, without double quotes. Leave it empty for an open server.

variables.name: SuperUser password
variables.description: Sets the SuperUser account's password at every start. Leave it empty to keep the one printed on the first start.

variables.name: Welcome message
variables.description: The message people see when they join, without double quotes. It can use simple HTML.
